MEK1/JNK inhibitors reduce, while PI3K‐AKT inhibitors increase IL‐1β production from macrophages from ascites of cirrhosis.
MEK1, p38 MAPK and JNK inhibition reduces the release of IL‐1B from M‐DM, while the PI3K inhibitor enhances it.

the identification of potential therapeutic targets for the control of inflammation in liver cirrhosis.
the role of the MEK1, JNK, p38 MAPK and PI3K signalling pathways in the secretion of IL1B in M‐DM obtained from the ascitic fluid of cirrhotics.
the identification of novel targets to reduce the inflammatory process in the ascites of patients with end‐stage liver disease.

PI3K‐P‐B inhibition increases the release of IL‐1b from peritoneal macrophaages from ascites of cirrhosis patients.
the inhibition of the JNK and MEK1 pathways is beneficial for the inhibition of the release of the IL‐1β cytokine in peritoneal M‐MDs, whereas the inhibition of the PI3K pathway is deleterious.
PI3K‐PKB signalling pathway is involved in the release of IL‐1beta in monocyte‐macrophage cells from the ascites fluid of patients with cirrhosis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PI3K‐AKT signalling pathway plays a key role in regulating the secretion of IL1B in peritoneal M‐MDs obtained from ascites of cirrhosis patients, while MEK1 and p38 MAPK signalling pathways play a regulatory role in controlling the expression of IL‐B in these cells.
the PI3K–protein kinase B pathway is a key player in the regulation of IL‐1 secretion in peritoneal M‐MD from ascites of patients with cirrhosis.
MEK1, JNK and p38 inhibitors are good therapeutic tools for pharmaceutical treatment to diminish the inflammatory response in cirrhotic ascites, but not PI3K inhibitors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MEK1‐ and JNK‐protein kinase inhibitors may be useful for the treatment of liver failure by reducing the IL‐1β‐mediated inflammatory response.
PI3K‐AKT pathway is an important player in the regulation of IL1B gene expression in macrophages.

PI3K‐Akt signalling plays an important role in the regulation of the release of IL‐1 in M‐DM from cirrhotic ascites, and that the inhibition of PI3‐Akt pathway may have therapeutic implications for the control of inflammation in cirrhotic disease.
